stages.label: SILICON ROOT
stages.detail: Manufacturer root CA. The attestation key is fused into the die and every quote chains back here.
stages.honest: Trusted anchor — the vendor's key-provisioning infrastructure.
stages.forged: Still the anchor. TEE.fail doesn't break the root — it extracts a key that chains to it.

stages.label: CPU TEE
stages.detail: TDX measures firmware, kernel and the inference server, then signs a quote that binds an ephemeral application key in its user-data field.
stages.honest: Measurement matches expected code; the quote is signed by a genuine fused key.
stages.forged: A DDR5 bus interposer (< $1,000) reads the key from one signing op, then forges a quote for the attacker's own app key.

stages.label: GPU
stages.detail: An H100 in confidential-computing mode produces its own attestation, verified by the VM before the device is trusted. Throughput overhead under 7%.
stages.honest: Device attests; the VM verifies and trusts the GPU.
stages.forged: Void. GPU CC anchors to the CPU TEE — a forged CPU quote lets an attacker claim GPU inference while running none.

stages.label: QUOTE
stages.detail: The signed statement plus a certificate chain walked back to the vendor root, verified once per enclave then amortized over every inference.
stages.forged: A valid signature over a false premise — it passes Intel's own DCAP Quote Verification Library.

stages.label: DCAP VERIFIER
stages.detail: Automata's on-chain verifier parses the quote, walks the cert chain and checks several P-256 ECDSA signatures, then registers the app key against the code measurement.
stages.honest: Returns valid → the app key is bound to the attested code.
stages.forged: Returns VALID anyway. The cryptography all checks out; the premise underneath it is false.

stages.label: SIGNED
stages.detail: Every response is signed by the registered app key over (model_hash, input_hash, output_hash) — cheap ECDSA, no new quote.
stages.honest: Signatures genuinely bind the attested model and its I/O.
stages.forged: Attacker-controlled: substituted model, fabricated outputs — and every signature still verifies.

numbers.label: GPU CC overhead
numbers.note: H100, amortizes toward 0 on big models

numbers.label: DCAP verify (zk)
numbers.note: checks run in a zkVM; ~$0.26 on L1

verifierContract.note: Automata DcapAttestationFee, deployed deterministically across Base, Arbitrum, OP, Polygon, BNB

verdicts.honest: Chain of trust holds — attestation is sound when the adversary is remote.
verdicts.forged: Verifier returns VALID — a TEE quote is evidence, not proof.
